statement: For SKU-level pooled ridge (alpha=1.0) forecasts using demand lags 1-4 and 4/13-week rolling means (no YoY feature, no promo, no trend, no category, no clip, no window), modeling log(1+demand) with a naive inverse transform (treatment) reduces WAPE of the next-4-week unit demand sum by at least 2.5% relative to the identical pooled ridge model on raw demand (comparator), estimated via two-way (series x rolling-origin) bootstrap over design B's 32 origins (weeks 110-234, 260-week history).
kills_if: Bootstrap 97.5% CI (alpha=0.025) for relative WAPE reduction excludes or falls below the SESOI of 1.0%, or the point estimate is <=0 -> drop this exact treatment as specified (log transform alone, no bias correction). These two conditions (CI-vs-SESOI and point-estimate sign) are the sole kill criteria; no supplementary qualitative criterion is used.
rationale: Re: the feedback -- the machine config given as authoritative and locked with this prereg (the one in this task's prompt) sets yoy=false for BOTH treatment and comparator ({"lags":[1,2,3,4],"rolls":[4,13],"yoy":false,...,"log":true} vs the same with log:false). That config does not add a last-year-same-4-week-window feature to either arm. So as configured, the comparator is pooled ridge on raw demand with the same lag/rolling-mean feature set and no YoY term, and the statement above is faithful to it. I flag this explicitly because the feedback asserts the frozen judge config sets yoy=true for both arms -- if that is true of the actual judge artifact (as opposed to the config text supplied to me), then the config supplied here is stale or mistyped, and neither this statement nor the previous draft's is being tested against the real judge; in that case the fix is not to silently add yoy to my stated comparator but to get a corrected, internally-consistent machine config from the PI before re-locking, since I cannot verify the judge's actual code from a config string. I am not preregistering a yoy=true-vs-yoy=true contrast on the strength of the feedback alone, because (a) the config in hand says false for both, and (b) even if both arms did carry an identical YoY term, that would still leave the treatment/comparator contrast on log vs raw demand structurally unchanged -- YoY would just be a shared control feature, not a distinct hypothesis -- so it wouldn't invalidate the statement's causal contrast the way the feedback implies; it would just require restating both arms' feature lists to include it. The user's own request text separately floated adding last-year's demand over the same 4-week window as a new feature; that remains a distinct hypothesis (a YoY feature addition, tested by comparing yoy:false vs yoy:true within one link function) and is not folded into this log-link test, consistent with revision 1. Design B (32 origins, ~5x compute) is retained over A (6 origins, underpowered for a 1.0% SESOI against a 2.5% target at alpha=0.025) and over C (58 origins, 10x cost, not yet justified for a first test of a single low-risk representation change); escalate to C only if B's result is marginal. Mechanism and the dropped Jensen's-gap follow-up remain as in revision 1: log-transforming demand should stabilize the variance-mean relationship and let ridge fit lag/rolling-mean coefficients more uniformly across volume levels; naive inverse-transform bias on sparse series is a real risk but is deferred to a separately preregistered segment-level bias audit with an ex ante volume-quantile definition and numeric degradation bound, not folded into this test's kill criteria.
